reason: The wording holds; the locator does not match the edition the source names. Read the 1885 Macmillan first edition in two archive.org scans (india.history.resource.89293, title page Vol. I, London, Macmillan, 1885; and amielsjournal0000unse_p9u6): the three quoted sentences are word for word there, as the third and last of the undated thoughts after the entry of 30th December 1850, but the entry that follows is dated 16th February 1851 in both 1885 scans. The 17 February date comes from Project Gutenberg 8545, which is the SECOND edition (it opens with the Preface to the Second Edition; the 1888 Macmillan scan amielsjournaljou01amieiala likewise reads 17th February 1851). So the source line pairs a second-edition date with the 1885 edition, and the verifier’s evidence misdescribes the e-text as the 1885 book (it also counts four undated thoughts; the 1885 text shows three). The fix is small: drop the closing date, which is true of both editions, or keep 17 Feb. and cite the second edition. Everything else survives: shipped.js says not shipped, nothing near, Amiel 0 of 3, not banned; in scope (journal, 1885 translation of an 1882 to 1884 French publication); a good six-in-the-morning habit line; Diary is the form of the work; the quotation is three whole consecutive sentences taken from the end of a paragraph that begins In the conduct of life, habits count for more than maxims; source leads with the name, no dash, under 140. Grep of First Light js data found no other rendering of the passage.
